channel.title: Updated · Biology
channel.description: Life sciences: discoveries, medicine and biotech

item.title: Lp(a)-lowering drug pelacarsen cuts the target by 78% but not heart attacks or strokes, in a large phase 3 trial
item.description: In Lp(a)HORIZON, pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a) by about 78% in over 8,300 people with heart disease, yet heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths occurred at the same rate as on placebo. (American Heart Association, Healio, American College of Cardiology)

item.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
item.description: In a randomized trial of about 1,880 adults over 70 without heart disease, stopping statins was statistically noninferior over two years, but cardiovascular events were more frequent over longer follow-up. item.title: Noise pollution alters the body or behavior of 80% of animal species studied, a Science analysis finds
item.description: A pooled analysis of 214 experiments on 177 species found human-made noise changed physiology or behavior in eight of ten species and cut animal numbers by about 37% in noisy areas. (Phys.org, Science (study DOI))

item.title: Parkinson's may be driven by a vicious cycle that clogs the brain's waste drainage
item.description: Misfolded alpha-synuclein appears to inflame the lymphatic vessels that drain the brain, which then clear it less well, in human tissue and mice. (New Scientist, Journal of Experimental Medicine (study))

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
item.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients. (FDA, Johnson & Johnson (OrigAMI-4 results release))

item.title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
item.description: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science. (University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American)

item.title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
item.description: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment. (The Guardian, ECDC)

item.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
item.description: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations. (Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University)

item.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
item.description: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species. (Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University)

item.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
item.description: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. (Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.)

item.title: First measles death in New York State in 30 years
item.description: A child in Lewis County, New York, died of measles, the state's first measles death in 30 years, as US cases reach their highest level in about 35 years. (The Guardian, CIDRAP, Gothamist, WRGB (CBS6 Albany))

item.title: FDA finalizes potency guidance for cell and gene therapies
item.description: The FDA issued final guidance telling makers of cell and gene therapies to build a plan proving that every batch is potent before it reaches a patient. (FDA)

item.title: English A&Es to use early warning scores for sick children
item.description: NHS England is introducing a vital-signs scoring system for children in emergency departments this winter, with parents' concerns able to trigger urgent review regardless of score. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
item.description: In a randomized trial of 744 older adults with moderate aortic stenosis and risk features, early valve replacement cut two-year death or heart failure events from 23.9% to 16.7%.
